text:
elyse: quick heads-up — did a targeted perf sweep across kernel candidates + mb sizing for streaming chat vs non-streaming completions. found a surprising p99 cliff when streaming_mb=8 on nodes with mixed kernels.
rahul: cliff? numbers?
perf-bot: raw snapshot (baseline hw pool x4, model rdx-3b-quant):
  streaming mb=4  : p50 15ms p95 95ms  p99 180ms  throughput 620 tps
  streaming mb=8  : p50 18ms p95 210ms p99 490ms  throughput 1050 tps
  completions mb=8: p50 22ms p95 120ms p99 260ms  throughput 980 tps
  completions mb=12: p50 27ms p95 160ms p99 320ms  throughput 1300 tps
elyse: notice the asymmetry — streaming p99 jumps much more than completions when we increase mb. tail seems tied to kernel fallback and KV cache miss amplification.
mario: what kernel path was chosen for those runs?
perf-bot: kernel selector logs: most streaming requests went to fused-attn-v2 until sequence_len>256 then fallback to generic-attn with higher latency. fallback frequency correlated with kv-evict spikes.
sam: kv-evict spikes? why for streaming specifically?
elyse: streaming chat keeps many active short sessions; KV cache churn + continuous-batching at mb=8 causes more interleaved keys, which trips eviction heuristics on nodes with limited KV slots. evictions produce cold KV lookups that hit fallback kernel hot path.
rahul: so two levers: mb-size and kv allocation/eviction heuristic. also kernel selector threshold for seq_len. could adjust kernel hint to prefer fallback-safe kernels for streaming but that hurts median.
mario: idea: split policies by route-type — keep completions at larger mb, but constrain streaming mb and increase kv-reservation per-stream. add hysteresis so transient spikes don't flip.
elyse: sketch of config I tested: 
```
runtime_policy:
  routes:
    streaming:
      max_mb: 6
      kernel_hint: prefer_fused
      kv_reservation_per_client: 8
      kv_prefetch_window_ms: 40
    completions:
      max_mb: 14
      kernel_hint: prefer_throughput
      kv_prefetch: true
```
elyse: with that streaming p99 dropped to ~200ms and throughput dropped only ~10%, completions unchanged.
perf-bot: ab run summary (A = current, B = proposed):
  A streaming mb8 p99 490ms -> B streaming max_mb6 p99 205ms (throughput -9%)
  A completions mb12 p99 320ms -> B unchanged p99 330ms (throughput +2%)
  kernel_fallback_rate: A 6.1% -> B 1.4%
rahul: solid. we should also instrument KV miss latency distribution and add trace tags for kernel fallback cause (seq_len vs kv_miss).
mario: I'll add a microtrace hook in runtime: emit kernel_choice_reason and kv_eviction_count in response trace for 5% sampled requests.
sam: can we make kernel selector prefer stable kernel when sampling shows high fallback risk? like a simple score = latency_est * (1 + 3*fallback_risk)
elyse: yes — propose short-term: per-route policy + increase kv_reservation for streaming; medium-term: improve selector scoring with fallback_risk feature; long-term: smarter kv-eviction LRU tuned for chat workloads.
rahul: action items: mario -> add traces + run 24h AB on staging (mb variations 4/6/8), sam -> prototype selector risk score, elyse -> open ticket and coord with eng-sre for gradual rollout.
elyse: opened ticket INF-4871 with config diffs and perf summaries. cc @eng-sre for canary knobs and safety limits.
mario: starting trace instrumentation now, will share perf dashboard link when ready :chart_with_upwards_trend:
sam: will push selector PR to branch mb-tune-kg and include unit tests for score behavior.
elyse: thanks all — target to have staged AB in 48h and update the thread with dashboards.
